title: Severed-wire audit of src/verification — turn-level watchdog seam + stop-hook infra (well-wired, minor duplication/dead-code only)

findings.title: VerifierChain::len() / is_empty() are dead public methods with zero callers repo-wide
findings.rationale: grep for .len() / .is_empty() on any VerifierChain returned zero callers (not even in tests). empty() is only exercised by a test; production expresses 'no verifiers wired' via Option<Arc<VerifierChain>> = None (orchestrator_init.rs + harness deps.rs), so none of these three observability constructors carries load. Read-before-write: no live caller anywhere => CUT the dead scaffolding rather than reconnect it.

findings.title: Byte-cap 4096 is duplicated instead of sharing the canonical LAST_MESSAGE_ENV_CAP
findings.rationale: LAST_MESSAGE_ENV_CAP (extension_stop_gate.rs:51) is the canonical cap but is a private const; stop_hook_verifier.rs:45 re-hardcodes 'let cap = 4096; // mirror extension_stop_gate::LAST_MESSAGE_ENV_CAP'. Two unsynchronized copies of the same fact (the exact single-source-of-truth smell phase 5 targets): changing one truncation limit silently diverges the other, so TOML stop hooks and extension Stop hooks would truncate final_text differently. CONNECT by exposing one pub(crate) constant and referencing it from both sites.

findings.title: The "end_turn" stop-reason literal is duplicated between the harness producer and this verifier
findings.rationale: The only stop-reason the harness ever emits is the literal "end_turn" (think.rs:936); MutationEvidenceVerifier compares ctx.stop_reason != Some("end_turn"). Its three sibling stop-gating verifiers (StopHookVerifier, ExtensionStopHookVerifier, ScratchpadGoalVerifier) gate on stop_reason.is_some()/is_none() and are immune to drift, but this one is string-literal-coupled. If the producer string ever changes (or a second stop reason is introduced), the verify-on-stop nudge silently never fires with no compile error. CONNECT by hoisting a canonical stop-reason symbol shared by both ends.

findings.title: for_behavior doc omits behavior_hint/vendor_identity in the resolution path it describes
findings.rationale: The doc (lines 39-40) states the behavior name is resolved 'via protocol_to_behavior / model_behavior_override', but the actual single source of truth is behavior_resolve::resolve_behavior, which additionally consults provider.behavior_hint() (vendor_identity -> "strict" for Kimi/Minimax/DeepSeek/Qwen/GLM). The omission understates the real wiring: a maintainer reading this could conclude weak-vendor self-identification does not affect the watchdog thresholds. CONNECT by re-pointing the doc at resolve_behavior.
